### What Vue Flow needs for nesting
Per the Vue Flow nested nodes pattern, each child must:
- Have `parentNode` set to its parent’s `id`
- Use `extent: 'parent'` if you want it constrained inside the parent
- Use `expandParent: true` if you want the parent to auto-resize to fit children
- Have its `position` set relative to the parent’s top-left
- Have a parent node with an actual size (explicit `width/height` or auto-expansion via `expandParent`)
Reference: [Vue Flow Nested Nodes](https://vueflow.dev/examples/nodes/nesting.html)

- • **Absolute vs relative positions**: Layout (e.g., Dagre/ELK/custom) computes absolute positions, but children keep those absolutes. For nesting, each child’s `position` must be relative to its parent: child.position = absChild - absParent - padding.
- • **Parent sizing not applied**: Parent package/module node either lacks `width/height` or `expandParent: true` on the children, so there’s no bounding box to contain the children.
- • **Creation order/race**: Children created before parents (or ids not stable) so Vue Flow can’t resolve `parentNode` at set time.
